headline: One year from DRS go-live, Exchange for Change opens registration and sets when a scheme barcode is required
executive_summary: This Monday-to-Monday week is a Deposit Return Scheme operations week, not a statute week. On 29 September Exchange for Change opened Phase 1 registration for producers and retailer return points, one year before the 1 October 2027 launch. On 30 September it published the first transition rules for PET and metal containers in England, Northern Ireland and Scotland: filled containers made before go-live sit outside the scheme and may be sold afterwards without a deposit logo, a scheme-registered barcode, a producer fee or a deposit; unfilled packaging that is not tied to a pre-launch order cannot be filled and placed on the market unless it carries both the logo and a scheme-registered barcode. That is the identification keep. Wales arrangements are still to come. The same day Exchange for Change named five logistics and processing partners; that is infrastructure, not an identifier duty, and is not a keep. Product-testing guidelines promised by September have still not appeared, and the certified reverse-vending-machine list indicated for early October is still unpublished. Construction and healthcare produced no new identifier, data-carrier or registry instrument. SI 2026/1053 is still the 17 October file. The toys-safety call for evidence, which includes the EU toy digital product passport and its QR-code data carrier, closes at 23:59 tomorrow.
cross_sector_themes: DRS has moved from countdown rhetoric to a live registration portal and written barcode/logo transition rules
A scheme-registered barcode is now defined as a condition of filling post-launch packaging, not only as a go-live artwork task
Pre-launch filled stock can be sold after 1 October 2027 without a DRS mark; members who treat every SKU as in-scope from day one will over-label
Identifier clocks outside drinks (NI battery QR from 17 October / 18 February 2027; toy DPP in the closing call for evidence; GB UDI still a December draft) did not move this week

sector_overviews.headline: DRS Phase 1 registration is open; transition rules say unfilled post-launch packaging needs a scheme barcode and logo
sector_overviews.summary: Retail’s two keeps are both from Exchange for Change at the one-year mark. Phase 1 registration, opened on 29 September at registration.exchangeforchange.co.uk, collects company and contact details only; product and barcode registration on the Scheme Article List is not this phase. Phase 2 is indicated for January 2027. Urban stores under 100 m² are automatically exempt from hosting a return point and need not register unless they choose to; urban stores of 100–199 m² and rural stores under 200 m² must still register if they want to apply for an exemption later. The 30 September transition note is the barcode file: filled PET and metal containers made before 1 October 2027 are outside the scheme after launch; unfilled packs not linked to a pre-launch order are non-compliant unless they carry a deposit logo and a scheme-registered barcode. Wales is excluded from this note. Logistics appointments, Scotland HFSS commencement on 1 October, and the still-open toys-safety call for evidence did not pass as separate keeps. Product-testing guidelines and the certified RVM list remain unpublished.

sector_overviews.headline: No new construction-product identifier, library or GSR text; BSR’s 1 October update is the building safety levy
sector_overviews.summary: MHCLG, OPSS and the Building Safety Regulator published no new unique-identifier, digital-product-record or golden-thread product-data instrument this week. The 1 October updates to higher-risk-building building-control guidance only add building-safety-levy material; they do not change how products are identified. Last week’s Manufacturers’ Information Hub proof of concept is not repeated. Government responses to the Construction Products Reform White Paper and the General Safety Requirement consultation are still indicated later in 2026. Official Journal citation of EN 18239 and EN 18246 has still not appeared, and the Commission DPP page continues to list that decision against September 2026. Construction exporters of batteries, or of products incorporating them, still sit on SI 2026/1053 from 17 October and the 18 February 2027 QR-code and passport clocks.

sector_overviews.headline: No new Scan4Safety, UDI or medicines-packaging instrument
sector_overviews.summary: Healthcare has no keep this week. The NHS Scan4Safety site posted the 17 September GS1 UK / PSC evidence report on 28 September; that is the same report already analysed, not a new development. MHRA activity in the window is routine licensing, an exceptional-use authorisations list update, a Class 4 medicines defect notification and a September advertising-investigations note – none of it a UDI, implant-card, MDOR or pack-DataMatrix change. Draft Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026 remain the December file, with GB UDI still indicated to enter into force in June 2027. A trade-press claim of a 1 October 2026 UKCA UDI deadline is not supported by MHRA or GOV.UK and is discarded. Trusts and suppliers should keep working the 17 September adoption evidence and the NHS Supply Chain Scan4Safety IMS framework, not wait for a new instrument.

items.title: Exchange for Change sets DRS barcode and logo rules for pre-launch PET and metal stock
items.summary: On 30 September 2026 Exchange for Change published the first written transition rules for PET and metal drinks containers in England, Northern Ireland and Scotland. Filled containers made before 1 October 2027 sit outside the scheme after launch and need no deposit logo, scheme-registered barcode, producer fee or deposit. Unfilled packaging that is not tied to a pre-launch order cannot be filled and placed on the market unless it carries both the logo and a scheme-registered barcode. Arrangements for Wales will follow.
items.what_changed:
Exchange for Change, the industry-led Deposit Management Organisation for the UK Deposit Return Scheme, published an update on 30 September 2026 setting out how producers, retailers, wholesalers and hospitality operators should manage the change from non-DRS product to DRS-compliant product around the 1 October 2027 launch. The note covers PET and metal containers in England, Northern Ireland and Scotland only. Arrangements for Wales are explicitly deferred.

Three classes of packaging are distinguished. First, filled containers made before 1 October 2027 are outside the scope of DRS and may still be sold after go-live. They do not need to be registered with Exchange for Change, carry a deposit logo, or incur a producer fee or deposit. Exchange for Change encourages industry to sell through that stock by April 2028 to support a smooth transition, but says that date is not a regulatory requirement and that in the vast majority of cases sell-through will be faster.

Second, unfilled containers linked to orders placed before 1 October 2027 would normally fall within scope. Exchange for Change is discussing possible flexibility with regulators that would allow non-DRS-compliant packaging to be filled and sold after launch if, and only if, it is associated with those pre-launch orders. Talks are ongoing; any flexibility depends on regulators’ agreement and has not been granted in this note.

Third, unfilled packaging that is not linked to an existing pre-1 October 2027 order cannot subsequently be filled and placed on the market. The note defines non-compliant packaging as packaging without a deposit logo and a scheme-registered barcode. No flexibility applies unless the packaging can be updated to meet scheme requirements. Further details are promised in due course. The same day’s newsletter restates these three classes and again flags that Wales arrangements, including any glass treatment, will follow.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1:
This is the first time Exchange for Change has written, in a public transition note, that a scheme-registered barcode plus the deposit logo is the test for whether unfilled post-launch packaging may be filled. That is an identifier and on-pack data-carrier duty, not a recycling-logistics story. The barcode types already accepted in the April 2026 material specification are EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A and UPC-E, unique to the product and compliant with the GS1 General Specifications or equivalent. Existing GTINs on in-scope containers still need to change and be registered on the Scheme Article List. This note does not open that product-registration form; it tells members which physical packs will be illegal to fill after 1 October 2027 if the new GTIN and logo are missing.

Two traps matter. First, filled pre-launch stock is deliberately left unmarked. Members who reprint every can and bottle in the warehouse as if it were in-scope from day one will create packs that look like scheme articles but are not registered, which is how reverse-vending machines reject valid empties or accept unmarked ones. Second, the unfilled-but-ordered flexibility is not agreed. Artwork teams that assume leftover labels can be used into Q4 2027 without a new GTIN are betting on a regulator decision that this note says is still in talks. If GS1 UK does nothing, producers will treat ‘scheme-registered barcode’ as a printer instruction rather than a GTIN-allocation and Article List task, and Sunrise 2027 QR work will collide with a second, DRS-specific linear code on the same pack. If members do nothing, July 2027 arrives with tens of thousands of SKUs still on the old GTIN, unfilled film that cannot legally be filled, and no Wales rule for glass.

items.title: Exchange for Change opens Phase 1 DRS registration for producers and return points
items.summary: On 29 September 2026 Exchange for Change opened Phase 1 of its registration portal for producers and retailer return points, one year before the 1 October 2027 launch. Phase 1 collects only core company and contact details and issues a registration reference number. Product and barcode registration on the Scheme Article List is not part of this phase. Phase 2 is indicated for January 2027.
items.what_changed:
Exchange for Change opened the first phase of statutory-scheme registration on 29 September 2026. Businesses that must register as a producer, a return-point operator, or both, can now create an account at registration.exchangeforchange.co.uk (also linked from the homepage as ‘Register your business’) and submit Phase 1. The fields named in the announcement are company details, primary contact, trading name and relevant business and mailing addresses. Progress can be saved. On submission the business receives a registration reference number on screen and by email.

Phase 1 is deliberately thin. Exchange for Change says it is designed to establish core business information and should be completed as soon as possible. Phase 2 will open in January 2027 and will ask for further information relevant to the applicant’s role. The announcement does not say that Phase 1, or Phase 2, is the product-level Scheme Article List registration described in the April 2026 material specification; that specification still requires existing products to be registered no later than 12 weeks before go-live (9 July 2027).

Exemption rules are restated rather than rewritten. Urban retailers with retail space under 100 m² are automatically exempt from operating a return point and need not register unless they intend to offer one. Urban retailers between 100 m² and 199 m² of sales area, and rural retailers under 200 m², may later apply for an exemption but must still complete registration now; the how-to-apply detail is promised in the coming months. The Grocer (30 September) and Talking Retail (same day) confirm the portal URL and the January 2027 Phase 2 date. Chief executive Russell Davies called the opening an important milestone and encouraged businesses to complete Phase 1 as soon as possible.
items.why_it_matters_to_gs1:
This is the opening of the identifier-keyed scheme register, not yet the opening of GTIN registration. The legal duty in the England and Northern Ireland regulations is that a person seeking registration as a scheme producer or a mandatory return-point operator must apply to the Deposit Management Organisation before 1 October 2027; the DMO may decide those applications early. Phase 1 is that application starting. GS1 is not named and is not the registrar. The connection is that the same organisation will later hold the Scheme Article List against which reverse-vending machines match a barcode, and that GLNs are the natural key for the producer and return-point locations this portal has now begun to collect.

The risk if the two phases are confused is operational. Members who treat a Phase 1 reference number as proof that their GTINs are on the Article List will miss the 9 July 2027 product-registration cut-off. Members who wait for Phase 2 before assigning replacement GTINs will compress artwork, production and RVM testing into the same quarter as Article List onboarding. If GS1 UK does nothing, Exchange for Change can specify a proprietary producer and site code in Phase 2 while members already hold GLNs for NHS, GDSN and PEPPOL. If members do nothing, January 2027 opens with no company record, no named DRS owner, and no list of SKUs whose barcodes must change.
